title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not stop after hitting the duck, which was nesting near a local restaurant. A resident claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing vehicle data.

This shows a gap between autonomous vehicle perception and real-world obstacles at the scale of small animals. The system either did not detect the duck or did not classify it as an obstacle requiring avoidance. A human safety operator was present but did not intervene. Whether the operator could have intervened in time, or whether detection or decision-making failures occurred, is not established from the reporting.

Avride responded by adjusting its testing area and running simulated experiments to improve obstacle avoidance. The facts do not establish whether the system was designed to detect and avoid animals of this size, or what testing conditions it had been validated under before deployment.

Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, did not stop after hitting the duck that residents had grown familiar with, as it was nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant. The incident gained attention after a resident posted about it on a neighborhood Facebook group, mentioning the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time and has since adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets near the lake. The company is now conducting simulated experiments to improve the vehicle's ability to avoid similar situations while ensuring safety performance remains unaffected. Meanwhile, concerned residents have secured the duck's eggs in an incubator. Other autonomous vehicle companies including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox also operate in Austin.
